france24fr.description: Les secours s'activent jeudi matin pour retrouver des centaines de personnes disparues, dont de nombreux touristes étrangers. Une crue dévastatrice a fait la veille au moins 165 morts et près de 1 500 disparus à la frontière entre le Népal et le Tibet, un territoire chinois. Les experts soupçonnent un effondrement glaciaire d'avoir entraîné la montée des eaux. Suivez notre direct.

france24fr.title: Ce que l'on sait sur les causes de la crue meurtrière au Népal et au Tibet
france24fr.description: Après la crue dévastatrice ayant fait au moins 165 morts et des centaines de disparus mercredi à la frontière népalo-tibétaine, les experts de l'Institut d'études géologiques des États-Unis suspectent un effondrement de glacier et une coulée de débris aux conséquences catastrophiques. Dans les jours à venir, les scientifiques du monde entier étudieront un potentiel lien entre le changement climatique et le drame.

france24fr.title: 🔴 Une voiture fonce dans la foule à Caen : 11 victimes, dont au moins un mort
Une voiture fonce dans la foule à Caen : un mort et 10 blessés, le suspect arrêté
france24fr.description: Un automobiliste a "délibérément" foncé mercredi soir tard sur la foule près d'un bar de Caen, en Normandie, faisant au moins un mort et 10 blessés, selon les pompiers. Les faits se sont produits après une bagarre et le suspect a été interpellé, selon une source policière. La piste terroriste n'est pas envisagée à ce stade.

france24fr.title: Les États-Unis approuvent le Rasonque, un traitement prometteur contre le cancer du pancréas
france24fr.description: Les États-Unis ont approuvé mercredi un médicament, le Rasonque, considéré par les experts comme l'avancée la plus significative jamais connue dans la lutte contre le cancer du pancréas. Ce traitement en comprimés permettra d'allonger la durée de vie des malades.

france24fr.title: En Algérie, des feux de forêt font au moins 12 morts dans l'est du pays
france24fr.description: L'Algérie n'est pas épargnée par les feux de forêt estivaux : au moins 12 personnes ont péri mercredi dans des incendies près de la ville de Béjaia, dans le nord-est du pays. Plusieurs autres personnes ont été blessées et de nombreuses familles ont été évacuées.

france24fr.title: 🔴 Ligue des champions : Lyon échoue à se qualifier pour la C1, battu à domicile par Fenerbahçe
Ligue des champions : Lyon échoue à se qualifier pour la C1, battu à domicile par Fenerbahçe
france24fr.description: Battu mercredi en barrage retour sur la pelouse du Groupama Stadium, l'Olympique lyonnais a vu s'envoler ses rêves de devenir la quatrième équipe française à disputer la Ligue des champions cette saison. La perte financière s'annonce lourde pour le club confronté à une situation financière délicate.

france24fr.title: Népal - Tibet : torrents de boue, bâtiments submergés… les images des crues meurtrières
france24fr.description: Au moins 165 personnes sont mortes dans une crue dévastatrice à la frontière entre le Népal et le Tibet, mercredi, selon un dernier bilan. Des centaines de personnes, dont de nombreux touristes, sont encore portées disparues et activement recherchées par les services de secours.

france24fr.title: Sénégal: la proposition de loi sur l'encadrement des fonds spéciaux invalidée
france24fr.description: Au Sénégal, le Conseil constitutionnel a invalidé ce mardi la proposition de loi du Pastef, le parti d'Ousmane Sonko sur l'encadrement des fonds spéciaux. Ces fonds de plusieurs milliards de Fcfa destinés aux présidents d'institutions sont exécutés jusqu'ici dans l'opacité sans aucune forme de contrôle. Le Pastef d'Ousmane Sonko et Kiiraay le parti du Président Bassirou Diomaye Faye s'accusent mutuellement.

france24fr.title: Ce que l'on sait des discussions entre Oman et l'Iran sur le détroit d'Ormuz
france24fr.description: Oman et Téhéran ont discuté, mercredi, d'un "couloir temporaire" de navigation dans le détroit d'Ormuz et de son déminage. Les Gardiens de la révolution ont annoncé que des accords avaient été conclus, notamment sur un partage des revenus liés à la navigation dans ce passage maritime. France 24 fait le point sur ces nouvelles négociations.

france24fr.title: Tchad : l’extraction de sable menace le fleuve Chari
france24fr.description: Au Tchad, l’extraction de sable dans des carrières qui longent le fleuve Chari met en péril le cours d’eau et l’environnement alentour. C’est pour cette raison que le ministère des Mines a interdit cette activité. Mais cette décision ne plaît pas à tout le monde.

france24fr.title: Ebola : l'OMS alerte et réclame davantage de moyens face à l'épidémie en RDC
france24fr.description: 🇨🇩 En République démocratique du Congo, la propagation de l’épidémie d’Ebola inquiète les acteurs humanitaires. Selon l’OMS, une personne meurt d’Ebola toutes les 30 minutes.

france24fr.title: Avec le réchauffement climatique, l'avenir du vin est-il au Nord ?
france24fr.description: Dans les pays viticoles comme la France, la vigne souffre du réchauffement climatique, phénomène qui déplace vers le nord des températures d'ordinaire observées plus au sud. Faut-il envisager l’avenir du vin dans les pays nordiques ? Une question que nous avons posée à Sophian Aubin de la rédaction de France 24.

spiegel.title: Magersucht oder Bulimie: Wie geht es Frauen, die eine Essstörung hinter sich haben?
spiegel.description: Was bleibt zurück, wenn jemand eine Magersucht oder Bulimie überwunden hat? Was ist problematisch, was hilft? Fünf Frauen im Alter zwischen 20 und 70 Jahren erzählen.

spiegel.description: Nicht ein Erdstoß, sondern ein Gletscherabbruch soll die Ursache der tödlichen Flutwelle in Nepal gewesen sein, berichtet die Erdbebenwarte USGS. Mindestens 165 Menschen sind tot, Hunderte Menschen werden noch vermisst – darunter mehr als 800 Touristen.

spiegel.description: Horrende Lebensmittelpreise plagen die US-Bevölkerung. Den Republikanern könnten sie die Midterms verhageln. Nun steuert das Weiße Haus gegen. Doch die jüngste Maßnahme verprellt eine wichtige Wählergruppe.

spiegel.description: Der Spätsommer gibt alles, doch so ganz kann er die nahende Kaltfront nicht bezwingen. Auf Sonne und Wärme folgen heute teils kräftige Gewitter. Vor allem im Westen des Landes heißt es: den Himmel im Blick behalten.

spiegel.description: Die USA wollen künftig alle, die Handel mit Iran betreiben, ebenfalls mit Sanktionen bestrafen. Iran reagiert mit einem empörten Brief an die Vereinten Nationen und warnt vor einer humanitären Krise.

nzz.description: Immer häufiger wird im Namen des «Gemeinwohls», «unserer Demokratie» oder ähnlicher Formeln gehandelt. Was wie die Verteidigung der Verfassung erscheint, erweist sich bei näherem Hinsehen als deren Umdeutung im Eigeninteresse.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Ein Glücksritter in Nöten: An Iran könnte Trump zugrunde gehen, nicht aber der Trumpismus
nzz.description: Donald Trump will als grosser Präsident in die amerikanische Geschichte eingehen: auf Augenhöhe mit Washington oder Lincoln. Aber dazu fehlen ihm Weitsicht und Ideale.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Eine gute Nachricht für die heranwachsende Generation: Endlich müssen soziale Netzwerke Verantwortung übernehmen
nzz.description: Der Meta-Konzern hat sich aussergerichtlich mit amerikanischen Gliedstaaten geeinigt, die ihm vorgeworfen hatten, der Jugend zu schaden. Auf Plattformen wie Instagram kommt es zu Einschränkungen.

nzz.title: In den USA droht bei den Zwischenwahlen ein Briefwahl-Chaos
nzz.description: Um die briefliche Stimmabgabe tobt in den USA ein erbitterter Rechtsstreit. Donald Trump hat jüngst einen Etappensieg errungen, doch die Zeit zur Umsetzung neuer Regeln vor den Zwischenwahlen wird immer knapper.

nzz.title: DER ANDERE BLICK - Steinmeiers Nachfolge: Das Amt des Bundespräsidenten sollte kein Bollwerk gegen rechts sein
nzz.description: Niemand kann die polarisierte Bundesrepublik im Alleingang versöhnen. Sie nicht weiter von der Spitze her zu spalten wäre schon genug.

nzz.title: Zwischen Fischfangquoten und Finanzstabilität: Island stimmt über die Wiederaufnahme der EU-Beitritts-Verhandlungen ab
nzz.description: Befürworter einer Anbindung an die EU erhoffen sich wirtschaftliche Stabilität und Sicherheit in einer unsicheren Welt. Referendumsgegner sehen Islands Souveränität in Gefahr. Umfragen prognostizieren ein knappes Resultat.

nzz.title: Marinedrohnen vor Rumänien, Warnsignale an London: Russland verstärkt die Drohkulisse gegenüber Europa
nzz.description: Moskau testet die Verteidigungsbereitschaft von Nato und EU mit verschiedensten Mitteln – und denkt sogar laut über Angriffe nach. Auf die diffuse Bedrohung aus Russland ist Europa noch immer schlecht vorbereitet.

nzz.title: Der Datendiebstahl in Liechtenstein reicht bis in die Schweiz. Ein Jus-Professor sagt: «Gibt es einen Skandal im Ausland, schwappt dieser zwangsläufig zu uns herüber»
nzz.description: Nach dem Hackerangriff auf den Finanzplatz Liechtenstein werden erneut Forderungen nach einer Reform der Schweizer Familienstiftung laut. Doch es gibt auch Kritiker.

nzz.title: INTERVIEW - Der Stabhochspringer Armand Duplantis sagt: «Ich will in Zürich unbedingt Weltrekord springen»
nzz.description: Der 26-jährige Leichtathlet möchte am Donnerstag bei Weltklasse Zürich eine Show bieten. Er sagt, weshalb er wegen seiner Hochzeit eine seiner raren Niederlagen kassierte – und was die erstarkte Konkurrenz in ihm auslöst.

nzz.title: ERKLÄRT - Keine Angst vor Motorschäden: Wann sich der Plug-in-Hybrid lohnt
nzz.description: Kaltstarts sind bei Plug-in-Hybriden dank moderner Schmierstoff- und Pumpentechnik gut abgesichert. Doch es gibt Tücken beim Einsatz des Verbrenners im Hybridantrieb.

nzz.title: Ein Kuhstall als Klassenzimmer: Indiens Kakerlaken-Bewegung prangert den Zustand der Schulen an
nzz.description: Undichte Dächer, defekte Toiletten, baufällige Klassenzimmer, fehlende Lehrer: Indiens Schulen sind in einem desolaten Zustand. Für Premierminister Modi ist das Thema höchst unbequem.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Heimlich gefilmt beim Baden: Smart Glasses führen den Rechtsstaat vor
nzz.description: Sie machen es praktisch unmöglich, das Recht am eigenen Bild durchzusetzen. Wir sind nicht bereit für diese Brillen.

observador.title: Dragões e Leões conhecem adversários na piscina dos grandes
observador.description: Em Nyon, olhos do futebol vão estar postos em quatro potes. Braga e Benfica dão passo final em direção à Europa. Ainda, novela Palhinha chega ao fim e FCP garante por empréstimo regresso de Fofana.

observador.title: Nepal. 165 mortos, 2 portugueses entre os 1300 desaparecidos
observador.description: O somatório dos números divulgados pelas autoridades nepalesas e chinesas superam os 1300 desaparecidos depois da enxurrada na zona da fronteira entre o Nepal e o Tibete.

observador.title: Artista japonesa Yayoi Kusama morre aos 97 anos
observador.description: Yayoi Kusama ficou conhecida pelos seus padrões às bolinhas e instalações imersivas. A artista nasceu em 1929 e sofreu de alucinações desde a infância, o que alimentou a sua produção artística.

observador.title: Tufão Saudel aproxima-se do leste da China
observador.description: O tufão Saudel terá perdido força, e as autoridades apontam que vai entrar em terra em Zhejiang e Fujian. 54 mil pessoas foram retiradas no sul do país após o tufão Narra.

observador.title: Benfica defende dois golos de avanço no reduto do Aarhus
observador.description: A segunda mão do play-off entre o Benfica e o Aarhus realiza-se esta quinta-feira. Os encarnados estão em vantagem face aos dinamarqueses, após terem vencido em casa por 3-1.

observador.title: 7h. Marques Mendes pede consenso entre Governo e oposição
observador.description: Antigo presidente do PSD lamenta o clima de "crispação" que se vive na vida política. Ainda, PSP não se compromete com o reforço de 200 agentes da polícia para Lisboa até ao final do ano.

observador.title: Rússia ataca Kiev e outras cidades ucranianas
observador.description: As forças russas lançaram ataques noturnos contra Zaporíjia, causando pelo menos sete feridos, e também Odessa. Um petroleito foi atingido no Estreito de Ormuz.

observador.title: Três filmes para ver esta semana
observador.description: A animação "Coyote Vs. Acme", "A Amiga Silenciosa", da húngara Ildikó Enyedi, e "Na Companhia das Estrelas", a nova fita de Ridley Scott, são as escolhas de Eurico de Barros esta semana.

observador.title: Pais contestam férias de verão demasiado longas
observador.description: JN: Confederação Nacional das Associações de Pais defende que as escolas passem a abrir mais cedo para ajudar os pais. Le Figaro: Primárias em França podem impedir duelo entre Le Pen e Mélenchon?

observador.title: 6h. Cheias no Nepal. Há dois portugueses desaparecidos
observador.description: António José Seguro já enviou uma mensagem de condolências ao homólogo do Nepal. Ainda, 11 distritos de Portugal continental estão sob aviso amarelo para a chuva.

observador.title: Taxas euribor no crédito habitação: o que esperar
observador.description: Variações diárias são mínimas. Mas tendência de fundo mostra forte subida em relação a 2025. Será que a taxa fixa é a opção certa? Ainda o número de insolvências, que aumentou este ano

observador.title: Como atua e quão perigoso é o “Gangue do Rolex”?
observador.description: Nas últimas semanas, foram registados vários assaltos em Lisboa com um ponto em comum, produtos de luxo. As autoridades falam em “Gangue do Rolex”. Recebemos Bruno Pereira, subintendente da PSP.

observador.title: 4h. Cheias. Sobe para 162 número de mortos no Nepal e Tibete
observador.description: Há ainda centenas de desaparecidos. Só do lado do Tibete são mais de 550. Há dois portugueses desparecidos. Ainda, onze distritos sob aviso amarelo do IPMA por causa de trovada e chuva forte.

observador.title: 3h. Marques Mendes: revisão constitucional não é necessária
observador.description: Ex-candidato presidencial admite, no entanto, que pode ser positiva se for "cirúrgica". Ainda, diretor nacional da PSP não se compromete com reforço de 200 agentes para Lisboa pedido por Moedas.

observador.title: 2h. Ormuz. Os detalhes do acordo entre Irão e Omã
observador.description: Embarcações serão sujeitas a vigilância antes de entrarem no estreito e só poderão atravessar com autorização de Teerão. Ainda, Marques Mendes pede "humildade democrática" ao Governo e à oposição.

observador.title: 1h. Diretor nacional da PSP considera que faltam polícias
observador.description: Luís Carrilho não diz se a promessa feita pelo governo de um aumento de 200 polícias nas ruas pode ser concretizada. Ainda, Ministério da Saúde vai decretar serviços mínimos para a greve do INEM.

observador.title: "Mestre das fugas" da prisão albanês capturado em Tarragona
observador.description: Trata-se de um homem de 42 anos considerado muito perigoso e que se encontrava escondido em Tarragona desde que fugiu de uma prisão de alta segurança em Milão.

observador.title: Cruzes, os canhotos! Marx (e Maomé) na Casa Branca!
observador.description: Será possível que, nos 250 anos dos Founding Fathers, os EUA se tornem vermelhos?

elpais.title: El número de desaparecidos en Nepal y Tíbet tras la fuerte riada supera los 1.300, con al menos 165 muertos
elpais.description: Los equipos de rescate siguen sin poder acceder a algunas de las zonas más devastadas. Hay cuatro españoles sin localizar

elpais.title: La batalla por los espacios para alojar a migrantes alarga la crisis de Ceuta
elpais.description: El Gobierno avisa: cuanto antes se pacten lugares viables, antes se devolverán. Malestar en el Ejecutivo con Vivas, que rechaza usar los polideportivos y amenaza con encadenarse, calentando los ánimos

elpais.title: La guerra sin fin entre Marlaska y Robles
elpais.description: Las discrepancias entre ambos ministros por la crisis de Ceuta son el último episodio de la difícil relación que mantienen desde que entraron en el primer ejecutivo de Sánchez

elpais.title: El ‘momento tabacaleras’ de las redes: claves de un acuerdo histórico que marcará el futuro de las plataformas
elpais.description: El pacto entre Meta y 52 fiscales generales de EE UU reduce las horas de uso de las plataformas entre los menores y pretende hacer de guía para el resto del sector

elpais.title: ¿Y si le prohibieras a tu hijo adolescente utilizar las redes sociales más de dos horas al día?
elpais.description: Con el acuerdo judicial de Meta, entramos en una nueva etapa de las redes sociales, en la que se les obliga a adoptar medidas de protección de los menores mucho más estrictas como refuerzo de los límites de los padres

elpais.title: La extraña muerte de un matrimonio irlandés en el jacuzzi de una casa de Cullera (Valencia)
elpais.description: La Guardia Civil investiga el hallazgo. Los investigadores se inclinan ahora por un accidente. “Mi hijo, que es enfermero, se acercó a ayudar y le dijeron: ‘No hay nada que hacer”, asegura una vecina

elpais.title: Un agosto madrileño entre la radial y los borrachos
elpais.description: La capital no da tregua a quienes trabajan en verano y pretenden refrescar el sueño con las ventanas abiertas

elpais.title: Elogio de la ‘tiesura’
elpais.description: En España no sabemos hasta cuándo podremos parchear nuestro empobrecimiento, frente a una UE que también da signos de agotamiento

elpais.title: Eclipse parcial de Luna: a qué hora, dónde y cómo verlo este 28 de agosto
elpais.description: El satélite natural será el protagonista del cielo nocturno la madrugada del viernes, cuando la sombra de la Tierra lo engullirá gradualmente

elpais.title: Tras Lorca, Clint Eastwood y el abandono, el Cortijo del Fraile intenta recuperarse de la ruina para dedicarse al arte
elpais.description: La Diputación de Almería lidera un proyecto de rehabilitación del edificio, escenario del crimen de ‘Bodas de sangre’ y películas, en el que pretende invertir 25 millones de euros durante los próximos años

elpais.title: El campeón del mundo que dejó el baloncesto para ser multimillonario: “Ganar dinero se aprende, es como ir en bicicleta”
elpais.description: El coruñés Carlos Martínez, oro con la selección española en el Mundial de 3x3 del pasado año, es elegido por la revista Forbes como uno de los grandes talentos del mundo empresarial

elpais.title: La nueva vida de Blanca Suelves, la eterna chica Don Algodón: “Dicen que hay que reinventarse, pero yo soy siempre la misma”
elpais.description: Fue una de las mujeres más fotografiadas de España, hasta que a mediados de los noventa se casó con el duque de Alburquerque y se alejó de los focos. “Pasé de salir en todos lados a no salir y recuperar la libertad del anonimato. No me gusta ser conocida”, asegura la exmodelo, que hoy es ‘personal shopper’ inmobiliaria

elpais.title: La falsa superviviente del 11-S: cómo una barcelonesa creó la mentira perfecta que conmovió a los Estados Unidos
elpais.description: Alicia Esteve se inventó a Tania Head, una mujer que logró escapar del World Trade Center y que perdió a su prometido en los atentados. Kike Maíllo y Markos Goikolea reconstruyen su impostura en ‘La superviviente’

elpais.title: El precio medio de la vivienda en España alcanza por primera vez los 2.100 euros por metro cuadrado
elpais.description: El valor medio de las casas sube en junio por quinto mes consecutivo, según los registros notariales. Madrid y Baleares superan los 4.000 euros por metro cuadrado

elpais.title: Calendario escolar 2026-2027 en España: inicio de curso, festivos y vacaciones en cada comunidad
elpais.description: La vuelta al cole, las vacaciones de Navidad y Semana Santa, y los días no lectivos varían según cada comunidad y ciudad autónoma. Consulte a continuación cuándo es el inicio del curso, los puentes y el final de las clases en su región para planificar el año académico

elpais.title: Adiós a los gastos de gestión ocultos: Consumo actúa por primera vez contra una web que incumple la nueva ley
elpais.description: Una norma aprobada en diciembre obliga a mostrar desde el inicio los costes adicionales asociados a billetes o entradas, pero muchas compañías siguen sin hacerlo

elpais.title: Ferrovial cancela el proceso de venta de su planta fotovoltaica en España en plena crisis del sector
elpais.description: La multinacional suspende la búsqueda de un comprador y admite que el valor del activo ha caído por la bajada de los precios de la energía y la menor expectativa de producción

elpais.title: Cometas infantiles llegadas desde Gaza: el nuevo motivo para las amenazas de Israel
elpais.description: Netanyahu acusa a Hamás de estar detrás del fenómeno. Niños y adultos palestinos rompen los juguetes, entre enfadados e incrédulos, después de que el ministro de Defensa advirtiese de que expulsará a la población allí donde se originen

republika.title: Champions: formula, date e fasce. Tutto sul sorteggio di oggi
republika.description: Alle 18 a Montecarlo si apre ufficialmente la nuova stagione europea. Italia rappresentata da Inter, Napoli, Roma e Como, alla sua prima partecipazione. La finale si disputerà il 5 giugno allo stadio Metropolitano di Madrid

republika.title: Il puzzle di Luis Enrique
republika.description: Al Psg vige la democrazia del talento: non avrai altro idolo all’infuori del gruppo

republika.title: Yayoi Kusama è morta, addio alla “regina dei pois” che ha rivoluzionato l’arte cercando l’infinito
republika.description: L’artista giapponese aveva 97 anni. La nota del museo che ha fondato: “Ha continuato a dipingere fino ai suoi ultimi giorni”

republika.title: Putin vuole il colpo di grazia. Il capo della Cia a Mosca per chiedere al Cremlino di non attaccare i Paesi Nato
republika.description: La rivelazione all’indomani del viaggio del capo della Cia a Mosca: “È frustrato pensa anche all’atomica tattica”. Ma Trump frena: “Quella di Ratcliffe di routine”

republika.title: Gli Usa offrono allo zar l’alternativa all’escalation: “Stop ai raid sulla Russia”
republika.description: Lo scambio per evitare che la guerra vada fuori controllo prevede la fine dei bombardamenti incrociati sulle infrastrutture

republika.title: Ex agente della Cia: “I rapporti tra servizi sono utili, ma manca un obiettivo comune”
republika.description: Jonna Mendez: “Mosca non sembra avere alcun desiderio di intavolare un confronto serio con gli Usa, né sull’Ucraina, né sulla guerra in Iran”

republika.title: Il pacchetto per Kiev pronto da luglio, poi slittò il via libera. Meloni e i timori sul consenso
republika.description: I commissari erano allertati per il 5 agosto, riunione rinviata. Pesano la crisi benzina e il pressing da destra: la comunicazione vira sui generatori

republika.title: Quartapelle: “Manca leadership, Meloni teme di dire cosa fa”
republika.description: Per la deputata “il Pd sul tema non è mai venuto meno, mac’è un problema nella coalizione, andrebbe affrontato come primo punto sul programma”

republika.title: Crolla il tetto del mondo, l’alluvione in Nepal uccide centinaia di turisti
republika.description: Si stacca un pezzo di un ghiacciaio, onde giganti spazzano i villaggi al confine con il Tibet cinese. I morti sono almeno 165, oltre 1.300 i dispersi. Si attiva la solidarietà internazionale

republika.title: Pellegrini, camion e soldati: quel ponte tra le montagne caro a buddhisti e induisti
republika.description: La valle del fiume Lendhe, che fu teatro di battaglie, esodi di massa e riti religiosi, oggi incarna le ambizioni commerciali di Pechino

republika.title: Il clima cambia anche il sole: “Più rischi dai raggi ultravioletti”
republika.description: Uno studio internazionale rivela che dal 2016 le radiazioni UV sono aumentate: in Italia più 10 per cento. La causa: la diminuzione delle nuvole

republika.title: Aumentano i raggi UV: “Rischio melanomi e altri tumori se ci si espone senza protezione”
republika.description: Bisogna preservare la pelle con la crema solare, le magliette di cotone non bastano

republika.title: “L’Europa si sta tropicalizzando c’è il rischio di importare insetti che trasmettono la malattia”
republika.description: L’infettivologo Francesco Castelli: “Con il super caldo, le anofele più pericolose sono in grado di vivere giorni in uno scalo”

republika.title: Chi sarà il leader? La sfida Schlein-Conte e il dibattito clandestino su un terzo nome
republika.description: I nomi su cui punta chi spera in un accordo a tavolino: Gualtieri, Salis, Manfredi e Decaro

republika.title: Campo largo, il nodo delle primarie a ottobre
republika.description: Servirà almeno un altro mese per decidere su leadership e programma. Bonaccini frena: “Prima il programma, poi valuteremo”. Gli incontri alle feste dei partiti

republika.title: Frida Giannini: “La mia Sabaudia a causa di degrado e incuria sta perdendo la bellezza”
republika.description: La stilista ha restituito al Comune la targa di ambasciatrice della città: “Da gioiello di Pasolini e Moravia a centro di camorra e disservizi”

republika.title: “Per ora niente attacchi all’Iran”: Rubio lancia la nuova fase Usa
republika.description: Washington punta sulle sanzioni economiche. Mentre Teheran tratta con l’Oman e si prepara a resistere con le criptovalute e lo yuan

republika.title: I timori di una crisi lunga. Sul tavolo buoni benzina e aiuti a tir e furgoni
republika.description: Il governo si prepara a gestire la fine dei tagli. Si punta soprattutto a voucher per i redditi più bassi

nyt.title: Deadly Nepal Flood May Have Been Caused by ‘Ice Avalanche,’ Scientists Say
nyt.description: An initial assessment of satellite imagery suggests an “ice avalanche” from a high-altitude glacier sent a giant cascade into the valley below.

nyt.title: Secret Service Officials Said to Be Put on Leave Amid Internal Inquiry
nyt.description: The agency’s top spokesman is among those on leave, according to two Trump administration officials. The agency said three people faced a misconduct investigation.

nyt.title: New White House Counsel Isn’t a Yes Man, but He Won’t Say No, Either
nyt.description: Will Scharf has proved his loyalty to President Trump, even filming a TV ad in which he blows away documents from the president’s legal cases. His new role will be to provide in-house legal advice.

nyt.title: Meta to Pay Up to $17.1 Billion in Landmark Settlement Over Social Media Addiction Claims
nyt.description: The social media giant settled with 47 states, the District of Columbia and U.S. territories, and agreed to make major changes to its products over claims its platforms endangered children.

nyt.title: A Movement to Restrict Social Media for Children Has Taken Hold Globally
nyt.description: Governments around the world have passed or proposed a range of bans or restrictions on young teens using addictive social media platforms.

nyt.title: After Meta Settlement, Teens Divided on New Instagram and Facebook Restrictions
nyt.description: Young people said the platforms could be a space for gathering, but also a waste of time.

nyt.title: What Does $17.1 Billion Mean for Meta?
nyt.description: The Silicon Valley company agreed to pay up to $17.1 billion in penalties as part of a landmark settlement with states over social media addiction claims.

nyt.title: Yayoi Kusama, Japanese Pop Artist Known for Polka-Dot Paintings, Dies at 97
nyt.description: The Japanese artist’s polka-dot covered paintings, phallic sculptures and public performances caused a stir in New York City and Europe in the 1960s.

nyt.title: Yayoi Kusama Was the Avant-Garde Radical Who Became a Pop Icon
nyt.description: In her mass-produced ubiquity, Kusama became one of her own dots, spreading her image into every corner of our culture.

nyt.title: A Republican Attack Ad Used a Family’s Tragedy. Now They’re Furious.
nyt.description: Relatives of a family killed by a semi truck say they were not consulted about the ad, which connected the crash to illegal immigration.

nyt.title: Meet Dean Roy, the 15-Year-Old Running for Vermont Governor and Ready for ‘Impact’
nyt.description: Dean Roy, 15, will appear on the ballot in November as a third-party candidate. He said his generation’s concerns, like affordability and climate change, have been ignored for too long.

nyt.title: How Darline Graham’s Politics Compare With Her Brother’s as She Runs for Senate
nyt.description: Senator Darline Graham has spoken far more about her desire to support President Trump’s agenda than she has talked about her brother’s political goals — or her own.

nyt.title: Tim Curry, Star of ‘Rocky Horror Picture Show,’ Dies at 80
nyt.description: The actor’s gift for garish eccentricity was indelibly appropriate for the outlandish, cross-dressing mad scientist Frank-N-Furter.

nyt.title: As a Storyteller, Tim Curry Had the Gift
nyt.description: He was a blast to watch, whether playing a mad scientist in “The Rocky Horror Picture Show,” a butler in “Clue” or a singing King Arthur in “Spamalot.”

nyt.title: Prince William Is Still Silent About His Brother, Harry. Can That Last?
nyt.description: Years of long-distance division between Prince William and his younger brother will be tested now that Harry has returned to Britain.

nyt.title: How The New York Times Covers Harry, Meghan and the Royal Family
nyt.description: What led to the surprising return of Meghan and Harry to Britain? What will it mean? Our journalists, and many competitors, are seeking answers.

nyt.title: After Whiskey With His Captors, Cuban Dissident Lands in a Miami Maelstrom
nyt.description: The former political prisoner Luis Manuel Otero Alcántara is unpacking 4,000 paintings he brought to Miami from Cuba and dodging criticism from exiles who once welcomed him.

nyt.title: Dolly Parton’s Other Legacy: A Fortune Given Away, Dollar by Dollar
nyt.description: The country star supported early childhood literacy, disaster relief, the development of the Covid-19 vaccine and more.

npr.title: Official leading Trump's Gaza ceasefire effort criticizes Israel for its attacks
npr.description: The official in charge of President  Trump's ceasefire plan for Gaza criticized Israel for its attacks on the Palestinian territory and warned that the alternative to the U.S. proposal is the next war.

npr.title: Greetings from Karbala, Iraq, where millions gathered for a Shia pilgrimage
npr.description: Pilgrims came to Iraq from all over the world in August. Many Iraqi and Iranian pilgrims walked hundreds of miles in extreme heat to mark the event. Outside the shrines, the atmosphere is almost festive.

npr.title: Nearly 1,000 are missing in Nepal and Tibet after floods caused by a glacial collapse
npr.description: China's Xinhua News Agency said Thursday that mudslides in Tibet caused by a glacial collapse have left three people dead and 558 missing, while police in Nepal reported at least 162 were killed.

npr.title: Canada to hit U.S. with retaliatory tariffs. And, remembering music legend Dolly Parton
npr.description: Canada has announced it plans to hit the U.S. with countertariffs that mirror its actions "dollar for dollar." And, remembering the legacy of country star and icon Dolly Parton, who died at 80.

npr.title: Hospital nursery fire kills 14 newborns in Pakistan's capital, officials order immediate inquiry
npr.description: A fire erupted early Wednesday in a nursery for newborns at a major government hospital in Pakistan's capital, killing 14 babies, according to hospital officials and the government.

npr.title: More than 50 kidnapped as violent gang attack in Haiti leaves 47 dead
npr.description: It is believed to be one of the largest mass kidnappings in Haiti in recent years, and one gang leader is threatening to kill the hostages if authorities kill any gang members as they try to secure the community nestled in the hills above Port-au-Prince.

npr.title: Canada hits back at the U.S. with tariffs as the countries' trade fight escalates
npr.description: The measures come after President Trump imposed 50% tariffs on many Canadian goods and threatened more after trade talks broke down on Friday.

npr.title: 'Forget about going back': 9 years on, Rohingya crisis enters dangerous phase
npr.description: The world largely moved on from the Rohingya crisis. But the exodus has not stopped, aid is shrinking and a generation of refugees is growing up with little prospect of going home.

npr.title: Trump calls leaders to isolate Iran. And, SCOTUS backs Trump for now on mail-in voting
npr.description: President Trump is calling on world leaders to join his economic war against Iran. And, the Supreme Court is backing the president for now on his order to restrict mail-in voting.

phys-org.description: An interdisciplinary team of researchers has developed and demonstrated a step-by-step framework called Socratic Challenger that uses artificial intelligence to help undergraduate students cultivate critical thinking skills. phys-org.description: The reappearance of Budapest's "Rock of Starvation" is a visible sign of a drought months in the making. IIASA researchers have traced its progression from missing rainfall and parched soils to exceptionally low flows across the Danube basin.

phys-org.description: Green spaces could play a key role in helping cities cope with the effects of climate change, yet they still play only a minor role in climate strategies. These were the findings of researchers at Martin Luther University Halle-Wittenberg (MLU) and Justus Liebig University Giessen (JLU), who analyzed the climate strategies of 25 major European cities.

phys-org.description: Researchers at the University of Eastern Finland and the University of Oulu have produced the first chromosome-level reference genome for the Saimaa ringed seal. phys-org.description: As climate change drives more frequent and intense heat waves, plants face growing challenges to survive and remain productive. undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. proj-syn.title: Democracies Must Get Serious About Industrial Policy
proj-syn.description: For decades, Western governments have ceded the strategic direction of their economies to the market. proj-syn.title: In the AI Gold Rush, the Cloud Wins

That is why Amazon, Microsoft, and Google are in a league of their own, even compared to other giants like Meta and Nvidia.

proj-syn.title: Don’t Mess With Markets
proj-syn.description: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has justified his intervention in currency and bond markets by arguing that they are not providing a fair signal of economic fundamentals. But they are, and Bessent's willingness to peddle such nonsense may be the most striking testament yet to the sycophancy that defines the Trump administration.

proj-syn.title: Kevin Warsh Owes Us an Apology
proj-syn.description: After only a few months in office, the chair of the US Federal Reserve has left market participants disoriented and confused. His first address to the annual monetary-policy symposium in Jackson Hole is an opportunity to set things aright—or to make matters even worse.

proj-syn.title: Is the Trump Treasury Panicking?
proj-syn.description: With the federal deficit near 6% of GDP and the national debt surpassing $40 trillion, America’s fiscal position looks increasingly precarious. By trying to strong-arm the bond market rather than address the underlying problem, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent may have squandered his hard-earned credibility.

proj-syn.title: What the World’s Oldest Bank Reveals About EU Financial Integration
proj-syn.description: To fend off an attempted takeover, Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena has launched its own bids for two other Italian banks. The episode shows why EU policymakers should focus less on making governments surrender their influence over national banking systems and more on building a European financing channel.

proj-syn.title: The Age of Gated Recessions
proj-syn.description: Aggregate economic indicators are obscuring a widening divide between those enjoying rapid income growth and those facing deteriorating job prospects. The rise of AI could deepen this disparity, with certain regions and workers experiencing recession-like conditions while others enjoy boom times.

proj-syn.title: The AI Curse
proj-syn.description: Every sanction that ordinary citizens have ever possessed—the ability to withhold labor, taxes, sons, or votes—presupposes someone who needs what you can withhold. As AI infrastructure encroaches on Americans, they are learning the lesson of many resource-rich states: where there is no need, there is no democracy.

proj-syn.title: Where Will the Global Bond Rout Hit Growth and Equities?
proj-syn.description: In the US, the recent rise in bond yields is largely driven by structural factors like the end of the post-2008 Great Stagnation, higher potential growth from tech-industry investments, and greater private-sector demand for credit. Higher yields are more worrisome for advanced economies that are stagnating and innovating less.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s Korean Catastrophe
proj-syn.description: Donald Trump seems not to appreciate that deterrence depends on the ability to mount a credible defense. This makes the Korean Peninsula a more dangerous place, not least because 28,000 US troops are stationed in South Korea, which the US is obliged by treaty to defend.

proj-syn.title: The Dollar’s Outer Defenses Have Been Breached
proj-syn.description: The puzzle of why the Trump administration is so concerned with a falling yen has historical parallels not to the 1930s or the 1980s, but to the 1960s, when US officials feared that a crisis elsewhere could spread to America. With US bond yields spiking, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is getting desperate.

proj-syn.title: Why the World Still Needs Wall Street
proj-syn.description: Outside of the United States, all other financial systems face major constraints on their ability to absorb large financial inflows. That is why geopolitical multipolarity is advancing faster than financial multipolarity, despite the many reasons that investors have to pursue greater diversification.

proj-syn.description: Governments and economists have long viewed demographic aging as a threat to economic growth. But new research finds that labor scarcity encourages investment and shifts innovation toward labor-saving technologies, boosting productivity enough to offset a shrinking workforce.
